title: Plus or Minus in Front of Each Number

concept.title: Every number has exactly two choices
body: In front of each number you must write either `+` or `-`. This is a decision tree with two branches at every level, `2^n` leaves in total. A recursive function carries the **sum so far** and, when all numbers have a sign, checks whether the sum is the target.

Two different sign choices are different even when they give the same sum, and a number `0` has two choices that both keep the sum, so it doubles the count. In the same way as before, the running sum is passed **by value**, so nothing has to be undone.

statement: Given `n` integers and a number `t`, write `+` or `-` in front of every integer so that the total is exactly `t`. Count the different ways (two ways are different if they differ in the sign of some position).
inputFormat: The second line has the `n` integers.

examples.note: Of the eight sign choices only -1 + 2 + 3 gives 4.

hints: Every number has two branches: add it or subtract it.
Carry the current sum as an argument.
When all numbers have a sign, count 1 if the sum equals the target.
